questions.question:
For certain chemical reaction X→Y, the rate of formation of product is plotted against the time as shown in the figure. The number of correct statement/s from the following is

(a) Overall order of this reaction is one
(b) Order of this reaction can't be determined
(c) In region-I and III, the reaction is of first and zero order respectively
(d) In region-II, the reaction is of first order
(e) In region-II, the order of reaction is in the range of 0.1 to 0.9                            

[JEE Main 2023, 29 Jan (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
Region I

In region I, the rate increases linearly with time.
This implies that the rate is proportional to the concentration of reactant.

Rate ∝ concentration

This is the characteristic behavior of a first-order reaction.

So, region I corresponds to first order kinetics.

Region III

In region III, the rate becomes constant with time.

When the rate is independent of concentration,

Rate = k

This corresponds to zero-order kinetics.

So, region III represents zero order behavior.

Region II

Region II is the transition region between first order and zero order.

Here the rate gradually approaches a constant value, so the reaction does not strictly follow either first or zero order kinetics.

Such behavior corresponds to fractional order kinetics, where the order lies between 0 and 1.

Thus in this region the order is between 0 and 1.

(a) Overall order of reaction is one → Incorrect
(b) Order of reaction cannot be determined → Incorrect
(c) Region I first order and Region III zero order → Correct
(d) Region II first order → Incorrect
(e) Region II order lies between 0.1 and 0.9 → Correct

Given, \(14 x^2-31 x+3 \lambda=0\)
Roots are \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\).

and \(\alpha \beta=\frac{3 \lambda}{14}  ...(ii)\)
Also, we have \(35 x^2-53 x+4 \lambda=0\)
Roots are \(\alpha\) and \(\gamma\).

\(\frac{\beta}{\gamma}=\frac{3 \times 35}{4 \times 14}=\frac{15}{8} \Rightarrow \beta=\frac{15}{8} \gamma\)

On subtracting eq. (iii) from eq. (i), we get
\( \beta-\gamma=\frac{31}{14}-\frac{53}{35}=\frac{155-106}{70}=\frac{7}{10} \)
\( \Rightarrow \frac{15}{8} \gamma-\gamma=\frac{7}{10} \Rightarrow \gamma=\frac{4}{5} \)
\( \Rightarrow \beta=\frac{15}{8} \times \frac{4}{5}=\frac{3}{2} \)
\( \Rightarrow \alpha=\frac{31}{14}-\beta=\frac{31}{14}-\frac{3}{2}=\frac{5}{7} \)
\( \Rightarrow \lambda=\frac{14}{3} \alpha \beta=\frac{14}{3} \times \frac{5}{7} \times \frac{3}{2}=5\)

So, sum of roots \(=\frac{3 \alpha}{\beta}+\frac{4 \alpha}{\gamma}=\left(\frac{3 \alpha \gamma+4 \alpha \beta}{\beta \gamma}\right)\)

\( =\frac{\left(3 \times \frac{4 \lambda}{35}+4 \times \frac{3 \lambda}{14}\right)}{\beta \gamma}=\frac{12 \lambda(14+35)}{14 \times 35 \beta \gamma} \)
\( =\frac{49 \times 12 \times 5}{490 \times \frac{3}{2} \times \frac{4}{5}}=5\)

Product of roots

\)

The curve \(y=\sqrt{4-(x-1)^2}\) is the upper semicircle of radius \(2\) and centre \((1,0)\).

The region \(A\) consists of the entire semicircular part from \(x=-1\) to \(x=0\), together with the part above \(y=2x\) from \(x=0\) to \(x=1\).

The area under the semicircle from \(x=-1\) to \(x=1\) is half of the upper semicircle, so it is \(\pi\).

The area under \(y=2x\) from \(x=0\) to \(x=1\) is \(\displaystyle\int_0^1 2x\,dx=1\).

Since \(A\) and \(B\) divide the upper semicircle, \(\operatorname{Area}(B)=2\pi-(\pi-1)=\pi+1\).

Therefore, \(\dfrac{\operatorname{Area}(A)}{\operatorname{Area}(B)}=\dfrac{\pi-1}{\pi+1}\), which is option \(A\).

An implication is false only when its antecedent is true and its consequent is false.

If the coefficient of x9 in αx3+1βx11and the coefficient of x-9 in αx-1βx311are equal, then  (αβ)2 is equal to

In \(\left(\alpha x^3+\dfrac{1}{\beta x}\right)^{11}\), the general term is \(\binom{11}{r}(\alpha x^3)^{11-r}\left(\dfrac{1}{\beta x}\right)^r\).

The power of \(x\) is \(3(11-r)-r=33-4r\).

For the term containing \(x^9\), \(33-4r=9\), so \(r=6\).

Its coefficient is \(\binom{11}{6}\dfrac{\alpha^5}{\beta^6}\).

In \(\left(\alpha x-\dfrac{1}{\beta x^3}\right)^{11}\), the power of \(x\) is \(11-r-3r=11-4r\).

For the term containing \(x^{-9}\), \(11-4r=-9\), so \(r=5\).

Its coefficient is \(\binom{11}{5}\alpha^6\left(-\dfrac{1}{\beta}\right)^5=-\binom{11}{5}\dfrac{\alpha^6}{\beta^5}\).

Equating the coefficients and using \(\binom{11}{6}=\binom{11}{5}\),

we get \(\dfrac{\alpha^5}{\beta^6}=-\dfrac{\alpha^6}{\beta^5}\).

Multiplying by \(\dfrac{\beta^6}{\alpha^5}\),

we get \(1=-\alpha\beta\).

Therefore, \(\alpha\beta=-1\).

Hence \((\alpha\beta)^2=1\).
